children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I have a child - Alex, who's 8 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have a child named Alex who is 8 years old.

To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Are you responsible for Alex? For example, do you live with Alex, or are you paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after them - such as for food, clothes or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me at the moment, but I do contribute towards their upkeep. I pay for things like clothes, school supplies, and help with their expenses - about £30 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. It's helpful to know you're contributing towards Alex's upkeep.

To better assess your situation, I need to understand this a bit more:

**How long has Alex not been living with you? Is this a recent change, or has it been more than 8 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has never lived with me yet - I'm actually in the process of adopting them, but they haven't come to live with me yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that - this is an important detail about your situation with Alex.

To assess your eligibility properly, I need to understand where you are in the adoption process:

**Has Alex come to live with you yet as part of the adoption placement, even if the adoption process isn't complete? Or are they still living elsewhere and haven't moved in with you at all yet?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, they haven't come to live with me yet at all. They're still living elsewhere while we go through the adoption process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have a clearer picture now.

Just to confirm one final detail:

**Is your local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance while they are living elsewhere during the adoption process?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. I'm the one contributing the £30 a week towards their upkeep.

Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that **you are currently not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

According to the Child Benefit rules for adoption, you can claim Child Benefit as soon as any child you're adopting **comes to live with you** - you don't have to wait until the adoption process is complete. However, the key requirement is that the child must have come to live with you.

Since Alex has not yet come to live with you and is still living elsewhere during the adoption process, you cannot claim Child Benefit at this time, even though you are contributing £30 per week towards their upkeep.

**The good news is:** Once Alex comes to live with you as part of the adoption placement, you will be able to claim Child Benefit immediately at that point - you won't need to wait for the adoption to be legally finalized. I'd recommend making your claim as soon as Alex moves in with you.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
